preview: Fardeen Khan shares his interview experience for the Technical Sales Associate role at Texas Instruments, detailing the rigorous multi-round process including online assessments, business case presentations, technical interviews, and discussions with senior leadership.
content:
Fardeen Khan - Technical Sales Associate
Final year Electrical-2024

Interview Experience

Branch: Extc, Electronics & Electrical
CGPA: 6+
No backlogs
Technical (20 questions)
Aptitude (20 questions)
There were two sections: 
Technical section had questions on core electrical, the questions were a mix of both analog and digital, questions on op-amps, filters, mosfets, bjts, transformer & priority encoder.
Aptitude was relatively easy with questions on quants- positions & directions, quick math, ratios, one or two questions on data interpretation and a few questions on logical reasoning.
Eligibility Criteria
Online pre-placement talk 
Online Assessment 
Technical interview 1
Technical interview 2
HR round
Interview with Hiring team head 
Interview with India Sales director
Roles Offered: Field Application Engineer(FAE) & Technical Sales Associate(TSA)

Hiring Workflow
Online Assessment

Around 18 students were shortlisted after the online assessment for the role. Before the interview we were given a business case study problem statement, a semiconductor company was facing a distribution issue and wanted a solution for the same, I proposed an optimized supply chain with ideas of reverse logistics, product diversification among distributors, breakbulk terminalization during seasonal peaks and a competitive analysis of that problem.
We were asked to prepare a presentation for the same and present it in the interview 1.
The interview started with my introduction followed by a few questions about my work experience at previous internships and a few technical questions from my research internship. He then started asking me questions on the design of a mosfet and then he made a mosfet circuit giving conditions of switching noise reduction, faults in output voltage and how to fix it, there were follow-up questions where he asked me the effects of connecting a capacitor at different location within the circuit. We then discussed my presentation of the business case study and he was impressed by my solutions, he asked me to provide probable solutions and sustainable planning on current semiconductor and electronics industry issues. He added follow-up questions to my answers, after he was satisfied with my answers, he wanted to test my technical approach and asked questions on how I would design a drone and how would I plan to switch a geo-stationary satellite covering x perimeter of earth with 10 smaller satellites covering the same distances. The interview went for an hour.
Concluding the interview he asked me what all do I know about TI and will I be willing to relocate, I happily replied yes :)
Technical Interview 1

There were two interviewers, the interview started off with my introduction followed by profile based questions- work ex, academic projects, position of responsibilities and a few questions on the academic competitions I had on my resume.
Interviewer 1 asked me questions on revenue generation, market cap, consumer demand, distribution planning and competitive sale and business dev. Interviewer 2 asked me technical questions on the working of a microphone with follow-up questions on how to fix a noisy analog signal and the sampling done from analog to digital signal.
Then they gave me situation problems, one was an angry client situation where I had a delivery issue due to the production issue on a factory level, they asked me how I would fix it and a revenue plan on the deliveries. Another was on rising consumer demand for our client and price negotiation for the supply components.
Later they asked me question about TI and why do I want this role.
This interview also went for an hour.
Technical Interview 2

The interview started with my introduction followed by profile based questions, it was a basic HR round where I was asked questions on how have the interview rounds been so far and questions about my extracurriculars, family background and future plans.
HR Round

This was a short interview, it started with my introduction and then the interviewer asked me to talk about myself apart from what was written in my resume, this was a tricky question since I had to frame an answer which would make me a great fit for the role and it was not supposed to be in my resume, I tackled that question by telling the interviewer about my experience with my family business led retail stores and my idea on opening a club.
The interviewer asked me to draft a plan on scaling an electronics retail store. He further asked me questions about the TSA role and why I wanted it.
Interview with Hiring team head

It was an online interview since the India Sales director was in Texas and he was working in US hours so the interview was scheduled around 10:30 pm. It was a 45 mins interview where he assessed my profile, my technical skills as well as my business solutions & communication skills.
He asked me questions on my internships and future plans. He asked me questions on my recent travels, we discussed about life experiences and where would I be willing to work, he jokingly asked would I be willing to work in the US.
Interview with India Sales director

Following are the topics to prepare for the TSA role
1. Analog fundamentals
2. Op-amps and filters (GATE level)
3. Case studies, Guesstimates & analytical thinking questions
Following are the links to refer:
1. For technical skills and technical interview questions - https://youtu.be/KBI7mGolOXI
2. For case studies and guesstimates - https://www.linkedin.com/in/verma-sarthak/ (he posts great consulting business cases and guesstimates)
3. For aptitude questions- https://www.indiabix.com/
Resources

TI is very selective with the hiring and each interview lasts about an hour atleast. They check each and every skill required for the job role. I highly recommend to build your profile with strong spikes in academic records, work experiences, academic projects, technical and business dev skills and great communication skills during the interviews.
